# AspectCut — Full Machine-Readable Knowledge Base

Canonical Entity Statement:
"AspectCut is a free, browser-based video aspect ratio changer that processes files locally with WebAssembly; videos are not uploaded to a server."

Homepage: https://aspectcut.com
License for Specifications: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)

==================================================
1. MATHEMATICAL FORMULAS & GEOMETRY
==================================================

1.1 Aspect Ratio (AR)
AR = Width / Height

Decimal Equivalents:
- 16:9 = 1.7778:1 (Standard HD Widescreen)
- 9:16 = 0.5625:1 (Vertical Mobile Video)
- 1:1 = 1.0000:1 (Square Feed Post)
- 4:5 = 0.8000:1 (Instagram Portrait Max)
- 4:3 = 1.3333:1 (Classic Standard Definition)
- 21:9 = 2.3333:1 (Ultrawide / Anamorphic Cinema)

1.2 Crop Loss Calculation
When converting between disparate aspect ratios with focal cropping:
- When Target AR < Source AR (e.g. 16:9 to 9:16):
  Visible Area Fraction = Target AR / Source AR
  Crop Loss Percentage = (1 - (Target AR / Source AR)) * 100%
  Example: 16:9 (1.7778) to 9:16 (0.5625) results in a 68.36% horizontal canvas crop.

- When Target AR > Source AR (e.g. 9:16 to 16:9):
  Visible Area Fraction = Source AR / Target AR
  Crop Loss Percentage = (1 - (Source AR / Target AR)) * 100%
  Example: 9:16 to 16:9 results in a 68.36% vertical canvas crop.

1.3 Even-Integer Macroblock Enforcement (Mod2)
Modern video compression standards (H.264 / AVC, H.265 / HEVC, VP9) operate using 4:2:0 chroma subsampling. Chroma channels (Cb and Cr) are sampled at half the horizontal and vertical resolution of the luma channel (Y).
Therefore, any odd pixel dimension (e.g., 1081×1921) breaks hardware decoding chroma phase alignment and produces severe rendering artifacts or decoding crashes.
AspectCut strictly enforces even-integer pixel dimensions:
Width = Math.trunc(Width / 2) * 2
Height = Math.trunc(Height / 2) * 2

2. VERIFIED SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORM SPECIFICATIONS (2026)
==================================================

Platform: YouTube Shorts
- Primary Ratio: 9:16
- Allowed Ratios: 9:16, 1:1
- Recommended Resolution: 1080×1920
- Max File Size: 256 GB (desktop upload limit)
- Max Duration: 60 seconds (up to 3 minutes for select creators)
- Codecs: H.264 / AAC
- Safe Zone: Top 15% clear of headers; bottom 20% clear of creator title, subscribe button, audio pill. Right 15% clear of like, comment, and share icons.
- Source: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/10059070
- Last Verified: April 2026

Platform: TikTok
- Primary Ratio: 9:16
- Allowed Ratios: 9:16, 1:1, 16:9
- Recommended Resolution: 1080×1920
- Max File Size: 287.6 MB (iOS), 72 MB (Android), 1 GB (Web)
- Max Duration: 10 minutes
- Codecs: H.264 / AAC
- Safe Zone: Top 130px clear; bottom 320px clear of caption and sound disk; right 120px clear of interaction icons.
- Source: https://support.tiktok.com/en/using-tiktok/creating-videos/video-specs
- Last Verified: April 2026

Platform: Instagram Reels
- Primary Ratio: 9:16
- Allowed Ratios: 9:16
- Recommended Resolution: 1080×1920
- Max File Size: 4 GB
- Max Duration: 90 seconds
- Codecs: H.264 / AAC

- Source: https://help.instagram.com/1037635830482480
